newsitem.title: JAPAN: National Sec aims for capital ratio above 200 pct.
newsitem.headline: National Sec aims for capital ratio above 200 pct.

text.p: National Securities Co Ltd said on Thursday it aims to achieve a capital safety ratio of more than 200 percent by the end of March 1998.
Earlier, the firm said its capital safety ratio at the end of March 1997 stood at 173.6 percent.
"We hope to recover a capital safety ratio of 200 percent as quickly as possible in the current business year," National Securities President Kikuo Noguchi told a news conference.
He said, however, that the company currently had no plan to ask its major shareholders to increase the brokerage's capital.
"We are confident that we will be able to improve the ratio by ourselves," he said.
National Securities will be able to post a profit in 1997/98 as a result of its restructuring efforts, including withdrawal from overseas markets and a reshuffling of its outlets in Japan, he said.

A capital safety ratio below 150 percent is considered an early warning level, and if it falls below 120 percent financial authorities can order brokerages to improve their operations under the Securities and Exchange Law.
Japan's Securities and Exchange Law requires brokerages to disclose the ratio, an indicator of their financial health.
